findings.explanation: `_time` is stored as UNIX epoch and cannot "reflect" a wall clock; `TZ`/`TIME_FORMAT` in props.conf only make the epoch correct. `strftime(_time,"%H")` renders the hour in the time zone of the user that owns the scheduled search (or the search head default), so a correctly parsed feed still yields the wrong hour for sites in other time zones.
findings.quote: Validate time zones: `_time` must reflect facility local wall clock because hour buckets (`strftime`) gate after-hours logic.
findings.suggested_fix: Say: set `TZ` in props.conf so `_time` is the correct instant, then make sure the saved search runs as an owner whose user time zone equals the facility's local zone, or (for multi-site) compute local hour per site from a `site_tz_offset` lookup instead of relying on the owner's zone.

findings.explanation: The SPL tests `hour < 6 OR hour > 22`, so grants between 22:00 and 22:59 are not alerted; the effective quiet window is 23:00–05:59, not 22:00–06:00.
findings.quote: Publish per-site quiet hours (for example 22:00–06:00 local)
findings.suggested_fix: State the window the SPL actually enforces (23:00–05:59) or ask the SPL owner to change the predicate to `hour >= 22`.

findings.explanation: The lookup is invoked on `door`, but the CSV as specified has no `door` column, so the enrichment step returns nothing.
findings.quote: Maintain `facility_hours.csv` (columns: `site_id`, `quiet_start_hour`, `quiet_end_hour`) ... `lookup facility_hours.csv door OUTPUTNEW site_id quiet_start_hour`
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `door` column (or a separate door-to-site lookup) to the CSV definition, and output `quiet_end_hour` as well so both bounds are available.

findings.explanation: description and knownFalsePositives (`count` over `span=1h`, keyed on `host`) describe an aggregation the SPL does not perform; the SPL lists one row per granted swipe in the quiet window by a badge holder not matching the allowlist.
findings.quote: grouped by `entity`. Outputs `count` each `the scheduled window`
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the real output: each after-hours granted badge swipe with time, badge holder, door and badge ID, excluding NOC, Security and Facilities.

findings.explanation: The scenarios are generic templates that do not apply to badge swipes. detailedImplementation already names the real causes (daylight-saving shifts, controller fail-over backlog replay) and others are obvious: approved overnight contractors or change work, staff on night shifts whose badge_holder name does not contain NOC/Security/Facilities, and late events replayed after a panel reconnects.
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `physical` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: List those causes and point suppression at `after_hours_approved.csv` keyed on `badge_id` or ticket ID, as detailedImplementation describes, instead of a `host`-keyed exception register.

findings.explanation: There is no `activity` field in the SPL or data sources.
findings.suggested_fix: Refer to granted badge swipes (`result="granted"`) during quiet hours.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `hour > 22` excludes the 22:00 hour, contradicting the 22:00–06:00 window in implementation. Also `strftime` returns a string ("05"); confirm numeric comparison works or wrap with `tonumber()`.

`NOT match(badge_holder, "NOC|Security|Facilities")` matches on the cardholder name, which rarely contains a team name; the allowlist should use a role/department field or a lookup, as implementation describes.
After-hours physical access is a security detection, not `Performance`; `splunkPillar: Observability` is likewise inconsistent with the SOC routing described in detailedImplementation.

SWIFT CSP CSCF 6.4 appears twice (regulation `swift-csp` and `SWIFT CSP`) with the same obligationRef. The TSA SD02C III.A (cybersecurity implementation plan) mapping for a badge-time rule is tenuous and the `https://www.tsa.gov/sd02c` clauseUrl should be checked. `detects-violation-of` overstates what an after-hours badge list proves for a logging-and-monitoring control.

The Authentication tstats has no filter for physical-access events (for example a tag or `Authentication.app`) and no hour logic, so it returns all authentications rather than after-hours badge grants.

summary: Implementation and detailedImplementation are substantive and mostly accurate (SC4S app ID is correct), but the time-zone guidance misstates how `strftime(_time)` works, the stated quiet hours do not match the SPL, an enrichment lookup cannot work as written, and description, false positives and compliance mappings are templated or overclaimed.
